items.title: GAUGE: When Not to Trust LLM-as-a-Judge in User-Simulated Evaluation of Task-Oriented Agents
items.why: Introduces GAUGE, a protocol testing whether LLM-judge-based agent evaluation gates actually correlate with grounded verifiable rewards, directly relevant to LLM-as-judge reliability research.

items.title: SynthSentry: Detecting Synthetic Data Contamination in Language Model Training Data
items.why: Proposes a corpus-level signal to detect synthetic/model-generated contamination in training data before training, relevant to data quality and model collapse concerns.

items.title: Zipbench: Low-Cost Framework for Compressing Comprehensive Benchmarks of Large Language Models
items.why: Presents a low-cost method to compress large benchmark suites into representative subsets without requiring costly per-sample results from many LLMs, an adoptable benchmark compression technique.

items.title: Tasks over Application Manuals: Revealing Gaps in Long-Horizon Procedural Reasoning for Language Models
items.why: New long-horizon procedural reasoning benchmark built from application manuals that exposes gaps beyond short-horizon multi-hop reasoning tests.

items.title: Harness or Model? Isolating the Harness Effect in Agentic Coding with a Contamination-Controlled Private Suite
items.why: Uses a contamination-controlled private coding suite to isolate how much agentic coding performance depends on the harness versus the underlying model, directly informing eval harness methodology.

items.title: MAxBench: A Multinomial Concept Recovery Benchmark
items.why: Introduces a benchmark for recovering multinomial (non-binary) concepts in activation space, directly relevant to steering and interpretability research beyond simple linear-direction concepts.

items.title: MP-Bench: Evaluating Voice Agents as a Multiparty Conversation Participant
items.why: New benchmark evaluating voice agents in multi-party conversations, extending human-AI interaction evaluation beyond dyadic chat settings.

items.title: Limits of LLM Text Detectors in Education
items.why: Studies failure modes of LLM-generated text detectors specifically in the nuanced case of partial/assisted writing, relevant to eval methodology for LLM detection tools.

items.title: KoSimpleQA: A Korean Factuality Benchmark with an Analysis of Reasoning LLMs
items.why: New factuality benchmark (938 Q&A pairs) targeting Korean cultural knowledge with analysis of reasoning models, a genuine SimpleQA-style eval extension rather than mere localization repackaging.

items.title: MMGR: Multi-Modal Generative Reasoning Benchmark and Evaluation
items.why: New benchmark testing whether multimodal generative models preserve physical/logical/spatial constraints, probing genuine reasoning vs. surface plausibility in generation.

items.title: SAEExplainer: Interpreting SAE Features with Activation-Guided Preference Optimization
items.why: Proposes a closed-loop method using activation-guided preference optimization to generate and refine SAE feature explanations, advancing mechanistic interpretability tooling.

items.title: When Auditors Fabricate: Batch-Size Degradation and Confident Hallucination in LLM Detection of Planted Document Contamination
items.why: Empirical study showing LLMs used as document-quality auditors confidently hallucinate detections of planted contamination, relevant to LLM-as-judge reliability research.

items.title: Countdown-Code: A Testbed for Studying The Emergence and Generalization of Reward Hacking in RLVR
items.why: Introduces Countdown-Code, a controlled RLVR testbed for studying emergence and generalization of reward hacking, directly relevant to reward hacking research.

items.title: Capable but Careless: Do Computer-Use Agents Follow Contextual Integrity?
items.why: Introduces AgentCIBench, an evaluation harness testing whether computer-use agents respect contextual integrity/privacy norms across applications, relevant to agent eval and human-AI interaction.

items.title: EvoHarnessBench: Can Your Agents Keep Pace with an Evolving Harness?
items.why: Introduces EvoHarnessBench, a benchmark for testing agent robustness as their tool/skill/agent harness evolves, a new agentic eval harness with adoption potential.

items.title: SAEScientist-Bench: Can AI Agents Conduct Autonomous SAE Interpretability Research?
items.why: SAEScientist-Bench tests whether AI agents can autonomously conduct sparse-autoencoder interpretability research, directly relevant to mechanistic interpretability tooling and automation.

items.title: Beyond Solver Verdicts: Generative Reward Models for Autoformalization
items.why: Proposes generative reward models to catch verdict-preserving-unfaithful autoformalizations, relevant to reward model design and reward hacking in verification pipelines.

items.title: SoK: Rethinking Jailbreaking in the Era of Agentic AI: Attacks, Defenses, and Practical Consideration
items.why: Systematizes jailbreak attacks and defenses specifically for agentic AI systems with tool use and memory, relevant to safety evaluation of modern agentic models.

items.title: EvoRS: On-Policy Self-Evolution of Reward Systems for Open-Ended Reinforcement Learning
items.why: Proposes on-policy self-evolving reward systems to counter reward hacking and discriminability collapse in rubric-based RL, directly relevant to reward hacking research.

items.title: Can We Trust LLM Judges: A Study of Capability-Dependent Biases and Multi-Judge Ensemble for Bias Calibration
items.why: Empirically maps capability-dependent biases in LLM-as-judge absolute scoring across 36 judge-examinee pairs and proposes multi-judge ensemble calibration, directly actionable for eval harness design.

items.title: Reality Is the Final Verifier: On Two Key Gaps in Agentic Software Engineering
items.why: Analyzes gaps between test-suite verification and real deployment correctness in agentic coding, relevant to designing more robust SWE-agent benchmarks.

items.title: Debiasing as a Measurement Intervention: Calibrated Ties and Resolution Loss in LLM-as-a-Judge Evaluation
items.why: Introduces TraceJudgeBench, a diagnostic benchmark showing that instructing judges to ignore presentation cues damages measurement resolution, a concrete new eval tool for RAG/agent judge auditing.

items.title: TREAT: Evaluating Access to Formal Knowledge across Equivalent Mathematical Representations
items.why: Introduces TREAT, a benchmark testing whether LLMs recognize theorems across equivalent formal representations, a novel formal-reasoning eval method.

items.title: Mr.LHDR: A Benchmark for Multimodal Real-World Long-Horizon Deep Research Agents
items.why: Mr.LHDR is a new benchmark for evaluating multimodal deep-research agents on long-horizon, dependency-heavy tasks, relevant to agent eval harness design.

items.title: Who Judges the Judges? A Chinese Safety QA Benchmark for Evaluating LLM Responses and Safety Judges
items.why: C-SafeQA is a new Chinese safety benchmark evaluating both LLM responses and safety judge models, directly relevant to LLM-as-judge and safety eval methodology.

items.title: Mr.LHDR: A Benchmark for Multimodal Real-World Long-Horizon Deep Research Agents
items.why: Introduces Mr.LHDR, a new multimodal benchmark specifically testing long-horizon, dependency-heavy deep research agent behavior beyond existing medium-horizon eval sets.

items.title: Overview of the NLPCC 2026 Shared Task 11: Agent-Based Experiment Reproduction from Scientific Papers
items.why: NLPCC shared task introducing AgentActionBench, a new benchmark for evaluating LLM agents' ability to reproduce scientific experiments, relevant as an agent-eval harness.

items.title: BenchShield: Formal Model-Backed Instrumentation for Reward Integrity in LLM-Agent Evaluation Infrastructure
items.why: Proposes formal-model-backed instrumentation to detect and prevent reward hacking in interactive LLM-agent benchmark infrastructure, directly relevant to reward-hacking research.

items.title: New Evidence, Same Choice: Testing Physical Experiment Selection in Vision Language Models
items.why: New benchmark testing whether VLMs know when they need additional physical measurements versus can answer from existing evidence, a reasoning/eval method for vision-language models.

items.title: Defining AI Agents: A Compendium of Criteria, Metrics, and Benchmarks
items.why: Survey compendium proposing structured criteria, metrics, and benchmarks for defining 'AI agent' across five dimensions, useful reference for standardizing agent evaluation.

items.title: An Open Recipe for IMO Gold: Training Nemotron for Olympiad Mathematics
items.why: Describes an open post-training and test-time-compute recipe (SFT+RL+verification) that pushed Nemotron to IMO-gold-level olympiad proof generation, relevant to frontier model and RL reasoning capability tracking.
